note.text: E-commerce is trade through electronic systems. Its vocabulary distinguishes stages: a listing describes an offer, an order requests goods, a payment record identifies payment and delivery supplies the item to its destination. An enquiry is not necessarily an order. A receipt does not alone establish delivery or quality. These fictional examples supply no real platform, price, transaction or consumer-law statement.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to distinguish listing, order, payment record and delivery. Builds on: context clues and conditional language. Leads to: quantity expressions and factual articles.

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original model: A seller posts a folder listing. A customer asks about size, then orders after details are agreed. The seller issues a payment record when payment is received. A later delivery note records arrival at the stated destination. The model distinguishes evidence without claiming every transaction follows this procedure.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Identify the action or document before choosing the term. Explain what the record supports and what it does not prove. Do not report an offer as a completed exchange.

cards.idea: Distinguish the ideas used in this lesson.
example: product listing: a description of an item offered.
order: a request for specified goods.
payment record: a record identifying a payment.
delivery: supply of an item to its destination.

cards.idea: Read the whole example before identifying its function.
example: The page describes the offered folder.
The customer requests the selected folder.
The receipt identifies payment for the order.
The folder reaches the agreed destination.

cards.idea: A correction must preserve the intended meaning and form.
example: A listing proves delivery already happened. Correction: Offer and delivery are distinct.
Every enquiry is a completed order. Correction: Asking for information and ordering differ.
A payment record alone proves arrival. Correction: Payment and delivery evidence differ.
Delivery and an online description are the same event. Correction: A description can precede transfer.
